## Why

ork (the owner's dashboard) wants to show a question raised by a role, sub-orchestrator or orchestrator of a slice relay, let the owner pick one of the provided options (or type free text), and send the answer back so the run continues. Today an orchestrator's owner-needed question reaches only its outer agent session; the ledger carries steps and phases but no question. ork may use slicer only through its CLI and JSON.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py:674-714` (relay-run step and list) and the ledger record model.
- The relay contract text in `src/slicer/ai.py` (`ai relay-orchestrator`).

## Failing tests

- `slicer relay-run ask RUN --step STEP --title T --option LABEL:SUMMARY ... [--recommend LABEL --reasoning TEXT] [--key area.topic]` records an open question on a step, and the step shows phase `ask`.
- `slicer relay-run list --json` carries `question: {id, title, options[], recommend, key, asked_at, answered_at?, answer?}` on the step.
- `slicer relay-run answer RUN QUESTION_ID (--option LABEL | --text TEXT) [--why TEXT] [--by NAME]` records the answer; `--get` (or `--wait`) lets the orchestrator read it.

## Implement

The relay contract tells an orchestrator that must stop for the owner to `ask` and then poll for the answer, instead of ending with a hand-back (a contract version bump; ork then adds the new version to its accepted set). Not in this item: any ork change or TUI.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-26: ask, wait, resume. `relay-run ask` records the question on the step and puts the step in the waiting state (s404). The orchestrator ends its turn with `waiting on: owner QUESTION_ID`; the outer session (or a dashboard) records `relay-run answer` and resumes the orchestrator with the answer. `relay-run answer --get QUESTION_ID` reads it. No `--wait` and no polling.
